lines: Home before the rows missed me. Thank you for seeing me back to the village.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I'll count that as good work.
I remember the relief of reaching a place with walls again.
You got me home without turning the journey into another disaster.
The first familiar face at the gate nearly made me laugh.
I slept through half the next day once I knew I was safe.
You checked the road ahead instead of pretending it was clear.
I noticed how often you looked back to make sure I was there.
The village seemed brighter after so long away.
I had forgotten what a door with a working latch felt like.
You let me set the pace when I was too tired to hurry.
We avoided trouble because you saw it early.
I was afraid to believe we had made it until the gate closed.
That journey ended better than I had dared to hope.
I came home exhausted instead of injured. I call that good guidance.
You shared supplies without making me ask.
The road was hard, but I never felt abandoned on it.
I trust you more because of how you handled that trip.
Getting home safely changed what I thought was possible.
I have worked through worse aches, but I should not need a <green><wavy>harvest</wavy></green> of bruises from one trip.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
I remember every step after the wound started hurting.
You slowed down when I could no longer hide the limp.
The road home felt twice as long once the bleeding began.
I was angry at my own weakness and took some of it out on you.
You kept checking the bandage even when I said it was fine.
I learned how heavy a small pack feels when you are hurt.
The first bed I saw looked better than any treasure.
I still feel that injury when the weather changes.
You carried more than your share so I could keep moving.
I was frightened the village would be too far away.
Every rest helped, though I hated needing it.
I remember the healer telling us we arrived just in time.
That trip taught me not to dismiss a minor wound.
I owe my recovery to more than luck.
You stayed calm when I could not.
I would prepare better before taking that road again.
We made it back, but I have not forgotten the cost.
Trust grows slowly. You cut yours down fast.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
You promised a way home and led me into danger instead.
I trusted you until your plan stopped including my safety.
You knew more than you told me, and I paid for that silence.
I still wonder whether you expected me to survive.
The road was dangerous. Your dishonesty made it worse.
I came back with less trust than I left with.
You do not get credit for fixing trouble you chose to hide.
I remember asking what was wrong and watching you avoid the answer.
If you want forgiveness, begin with the truth.
I will not follow another plan I am not allowed to understand.
Being used frightened me more than the journey did.
I had to protect myself from the danger and from your choices.
You left me no good way to turn back.
The village welcomed me home. I could barely look at you.
Time has cooled my anger, but it has not repaired the trust.
Next time, I decide what risks are mine to take.
I survived. That does not make what you did right.
I know soil better than water. The boat was appreciated.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
I was glad to leave, but the boat did not feel like safety yet.
You kept us moving when the current tried to turn us around.
I watched the shore shrink and wondered if I had made a mistake.
The first night on the water felt longer than it was.
We rationed food because neither of us knew the true distance.
I learned to sleep through the sound of waves against wood.
You spotted land before I did.
I had never been so happy to step into mud at the shore.
The boat leaked just enough to keep me worried.
We took turns watching the sky and the water.
I still remember how cold the spray felt.
Every distant shape looked like land until we got closer.
You kept the supplies dry when I could barely keep my balance.
The journey taught me how quickly weather changes over open water.
I trusted your rowing more each time the boat stayed upright.
We arrived tired, soaked, and finally safe.
I would take that crossing again if home waited at the end.
